definition: a feeling of doubt or worry about whether something is right

collocations.example: I had serious misgivings about accepting the new job.
She read the letter with a growing sense of misgiving.

definition: a feeling that you cannot trust or rely on someone

collocations.example: There was deep mistrust between the two rival managers.
Years of conflict created mutual mistrust between the neighbors.

definition: a tiny creature related to spiders that lives on plants, animals, or in dust

collocations.example: Dust mites in old pillows can trigger allergies.
Spider mites had damaged the leaves of the plant.

definition: a situation in which something is made to seem foolish or worthless

collocations.example: The unfair ruling made a mockery of the whole trial.
The quick verdict was a mockery of justice.

definition: the practice of keeping within reasonable limits and avoiding extremes

collocations.example: You can enjoy sweets if you eat them in moderation.
The leaders urged both sides to show moderation.

definition: (of metal or rock) made liquid by very high heat

collocations.example: Workers poured the molten metal into large moulds.
The volcano spewed molten rock high into the air.

definition: very important because of effects likely to happen in the future

collocations.example: Their wedding was a momentous occasion for both families.
The board faced a momentous decision about the merger.

definition: relating to monks or the life they live in a monastery

collocations.example: He was drawn to the quiet of monastic life.
She joined a strict monastic order in her twenties.

definition: a detailed written study of one particular subject

collocations.example: She plans to publish a monograph on medieval art.
He wrote a monograph on the history of jazz.

definition: a large organization that is powerful and seems unable to change

collocations.example: The small firm grew into a corporate monolith.
Over the years the bank became a faceless corporate monolith.

definition: a long speech made by one person, often during a conversation

collocations.example: He went into a long monologue about his childhood.
She launched into a monologue about her travels abroad.

definition: the boring quality of something that never changes

collocations.example: A short trip helped break the monotony of winter.
She hated the monotony of her daily routine.

definition: an oxide whose molecule contains one oxygen atom, as in carbon monoxide

collocations.example: Carbon monoxide is a dangerous and colorless gas.
Faulty heaters can cause deadly carbon monoxide poisoning.

definition: open to argument or discussion because it is not yet decided

collocations.example: Whether he resigned willingly is a moot point.
Whether the plan will actually work is a moot question.

definition: an official agreement to stop an activity for a period of time

collocations.example: The government imposed a moratorium on nuclear testing.
The convention called for a moratorium on commercial whaling.

definition: involving several political parties

collocations.example: Voters took part in their first multiparty elections.
The country slowly moved toward a multiparty system.

definition: a very large number or variety of something

collocations.example: The final outcome depends on a multiplicity of factors.
The report reflects a multiplicity of voices and views.

definition: to eat something steadily, often making a noise

collocations.example: The children munched on carrots while watching television.
He sat munching away at a bag of crisps.

definition: a small sea creature with a black shell that can be eaten

collocations.example: We ordered a bowl of fresh mussels for lunch.
She found an empty mussel shell on the beach.

definition: a situation in which soldiers or sailors refuse to obey their leaders

collocations.example: Poor conditions on the ship led to mutiny.
A mutiny broke out among the hungry crew.

definition: to confuse someone completely because they cannot understand something

collocations.example: The strange noise completely mystified the engineers.
His sudden decision mystified everyone in the office.

definition: to make someone who was born in another country a legal citizen

collocations.example: She became naturalised after living there for ten years.
He is now a naturalised citizen of Canada.

definition: the long central part of a church where people sit

collocations.example: Light flooded into the church nave through tall windows.
Visitors gathered in the central nave of the cathedral.

definition: a vote or answer of 'no'

collocations.example: Several members chose to vote nay on the proposal.
The board must decide the matter, yea or nay.

definition: tending to worry too much or behave in an anxious, obsessive way

collocations.example: He was almost neurotic about keeping his desk tidy.
She became neurotic about being late for work.

definition: a small amphibian with a long tail that lives partly in water

collocations.example: A common newt swam slowly across the pond.
The children spotted a newt near the stream.

definition: a small cut or notch in a surface or edge

collocations.example: He got a small nick while shaving this morning.
There was a tiny nick in the knife blade.

definition: a hard silvery-white metal used in making other metals

collocations.example: The parts are made from a strong nickel alloy.
The tap has a shiny nickel plating.

definition: an addictive substance found in tobacco

collocations.example: She used a nicotine patch to help her quit.
Nicotine addiction makes smoking very hard to give up.

definition: zero; nothing at all

collocations.example: My chances of winning were practically nil.
Our team won the match two-nil.

definition: a long thin strip of pasta used in cooking, often in soup

collocations.example: We had chicken noodle soup for lunch.
Busy students often live on cheap instant noodles.

definition: a narrow spout at the end of a hose or pipe that controls flow

collocations.example: He adjusted the spray nozzle to water the plants.
Water shot out of the hose nozzle with force.

definition: not expressed in a direct way; indirect

collocations.example: She made an oblique reference to his past mistakes.
He took an oblique approach to the difficult subject.

definition: the state of being completely forgotten

collocations.example: Many once-famous silent film stars faded into oblivion.
His early inventions were soon consigned to oblivion.

definition: the practice of obeying a law, rule, or custom

collocations.example: The club demands strict observance of its rules.
Observance of the law is a matter of principle.

definition: the branch of medicine dealing with pregnancy and childbirth

collocations.example: She specializes in obstetrics and gynaecology at the hospital.
He trained in obstetrics for several years.

definition: a fierce or violent attack

collocations.example: The press launched a vicious onslaught on the minister.
The town could not withstand the enemy onslaught.

definition: an addictive drug made from the juice of the poppy

collocations.example: In the past, many people smoked opium to relax.
The opium trade once caused serious social problems.

definition: a person who is skilled at making public speeches

collocations.example: The senator was a gifted orator who moved audiences.
As a fiery orator, he could stir any crowd.

definition: a law or rule made by a local government or authority

collocations.example: A new city ordinance bans smoking in public parks.
The council voted to pass the new ordinance.

definition: the ceremony of making someone a priest or religious minister

collocations.example: The church debated the ordination of women as priests.
The young man studied for years before his ordination.

definition: a furry river or sea animal with webbed feet that eats fish

collocations.example: A sea otter floated on its back eating shellfish.
We watched a river otter dive for fish.

definition: a strong expression of public anger or protest

collocations.example: The new tax caused a public outcry.
The decision provoked an outcry from local residents.

definition: no longer useful or modern; out of date

collocations.example: The factory still relies on outdated equipment.
Managers finally abandoned their outdated methods.

definition: an amount of money spent, especially to start something

collocations.example: The new machine required a large capital outlay.
The business soon repaid the initial outlay on advertising.

definition: a small settlement or military base in a remote area

collocations.example: They were stationed at a remote outpost in the desert.
The army built a military outpost near the border.

definition: an organization's effort to provide services or help to a community

collocations.example: Their team does outreach work with homeless young people.
The hospital expanded its community outreach programs.

definition: one of the two organs in a female that produce eggs

collocations.example: Many women are affected by polycystic ovary syndrome.
The scan showed a small cyst on the left ovary.

definition: over the side of a boat or ship into the water

collocations.example: A passenger nearly fell overboard during the storm.
Huge waves washed him overboard into the sea.

definition: a long warm coat worn over other clothes in cold weather

collocations.example: He put on a heavy overcoat before leaving.
She wore a long overcoat over her suit.

definition: to do something too much or to an excessive degree

collocations.example: Exercise is good, but don't overdo it.
He tends to overdo things when he's excited.

definition: to think something is larger, better, or more important than it really is

collocations.example: Don't overestimate the importance of a single test.
Young drivers often overestimate their own abilities.

definition: to grow over and cover something completely

collocations.example: Thick bushes began to overgrow the garden path.
Thick ivy had begun to overgrow the old garden wall.

definition: to become or make something too hot

collocations.example: The engine overheated badly after the long climb.
Be careful not to overheat the liquid.

definition: to use your authority to reject someone's decision or argument

collocations.example: The court can overrule the lower judge's decision.
The judge chose to overrule the lawyer's objection.

definition: to describe something as larger or more important than it really is

collocations.example: He tends to overstate the case for reform.
The report may overstate the risk of infection.

definition: an additional quality or meaning that is suggested but not openly stated

collocations.example: The speech carried clear political overtones.
Her polite words had a sinister overtone.

definition: an attempt to start a discussion or friendly relationship with someone

collocations.example: The company made an overture to its biggest rival.
The government rejected the rebels' peace overture.

definition: the state of working too hard for too long

collocations.example: Many employees suffer from overwork and constant stress.
He finally collapsed from sheer overwork.

definition: a large cattle animal, often used for pulling heavy loads

collocations.example: The farmer used a strong ox to plow the field.
Goods were carried slowly by ox cart.

definition: a person who believes that war and violence are always wrong

collocations.example: As a committed pacifist, he refused to fight.
After the war he became a convinced pacifist.

definition: to call someone over a loudspeaker or by sending a message to a pager

collocations.example: Why don't you have him paged at the airport?
The nurse had to page a doctor urgently.

definition: having a pleasant taste; good to eat

collocations.example: The small restaurant serves simple but palatable food.
A little salt can make the dish more palatable.

definition: the top inside surface of the mouth

collocations.example: The dentist carefully examined his hard palate and gums.
Surgeons successfully repaired the baby's cleft palate.

definition: (of a feeling) so strong that it seems possible to touch it

collocations.example: The tension in the meeting was almost palpable.
There was palpable relief when the good news arrived.

definition: to treat someone with great care and make them feel comfortable

collocations.example: Take a day off and pamper yourself a little.
Don't pamper the child too much.

definition: relating to the pancreas, an organ that helps digestion

collocations.example: He died in 2003 of pancreatic cancer.
Pancreatic juice helps the body break down food.

definition: a sudden sharp feeling of emotional or physical pain

collocations.example: She felt a pang of guilt about leaving early.
A sudden pang of hunger made him stop.

definition: a small room or cupboard for storing food

collocations.example: She keeps canned goods in the kitchen pantry.
They stocked the pantry before the long winter.

definition: a short story that teaches a moral or religious lesson

collocations.example: The minister preached on the parable of the lost sheep.
Jesus often told a parable to teach his followers.

definition: the loss of the ability to move part or all of the body

collocations.example: The spinal injury caused paralysis in both legs.
She sometimes experiences frightening episodes of sleep paralysis.

definition: an unreasonable feeling that others cannot be trusted or want to harm you

collocations.example: A sense of paranoia spread through the office.
The rumors only served to fuel his paranoia.

definition: to express something written or spoken using different words

collocations.example: Students learn to paraphrase a text in their own words.
To paraphrase the author, change is always difficult.

definition: a material made from animal skin, used in the past for writing

collocations.example: The museum displayed an ancient parchment scroll.
The document was written on parchment centuries ago.

definition: showing interest only in small local matters; narrow-minded

collocations.example: He criticized the parochial attitudes of the committee.
Their parochial outlook ignored the wider world.

definition: an activity that you enjoy doing in your free time

collocations.example: Fishing is his favorite pastime on weekends.
Baseball is often called America's national pastime.

definition: a tiny organism, such as a bacterium, that causes disease

collocations.example: The new vaccine protects against a harmful pathogen.
Dirty water can spread a dangerous pathogen.

definition: behaving in an extreme way that you cannot control

collocations.example: He turned out to be a pathological liar.
Her pathological jealousy ruined the relationship.

definition: a person who is used by others for their own advantage

collocations.example: He was used as a political pawn by both sides.
She felt like a mere pawn in their game.

definition: to try to sell goods, often by going from place to place

collocations.example: He traveled from town to town to peddle goods.
The gang was arrested for trying to peddle drugs.

definition: the base that supports a statue, column, or vase

collocations.example: The statue stood on a tall marble pedestal.
She placed the vase back on its pedestal.

definition: a history or background that gives something or someone good quality

collocations.example: The company has a long pedigree in engineering.
The car has an impressive sporting pedigree.

definition: to throw a large number of things at someone or something

collocations.example: The angry crowd began to pelt the car with stones.
The boys pelted each other with snowballs.

definition: a piece of jewelry that hangs from a chain around the neck

collocations.example: She wore a sparkling diamond pendant to the gala.
He likes to wear a pendant around his neck.

definition: a weight hung from a fixed point so it can swing freely, as in a clock

collocations.example: The child watched the swinging pendulum of the old clock.
An antique pendulum clock stood in the hall.

definition: a black and white sea bird that cannot fly but swims well

collocations.example: An emperor penguin can dive very deep for fish.
A king penguin stood proudly on the icy shore.

definition: a flat shape with five straight sides and five angles

collocations.example: The students drew a regular pentagon in geometry class.
The old fort was shaped like a pentagon.

definition: energy, enthusiasm, and liveliness

collocations.example: The coach gave the team a pep talk.
She arrived at work full of pep.

definition: quick to notice and understand things

collocations.example: She made a perceptive comment about the film.
He is a highly perceptive political commentator.
